chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him, 'The battalion which the Imam sends, so they acquire war booty, how is it distributed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If they fought over it with a commander whom the Imam appointed over them, one-fifth is taken out from it for Allah and for the Messenger, and four-fifths are distributed between them. And if they did not fight the Polytheists over it, everything which they acquired is for the Imam; he makes it wherever he likes.'

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَخْمَاسٍ: Four-fifths, the remaining portion of booty distributed to fighters after khums
key_terms.السَّرِيَّةُ: A military battalion or expedition sent by the Imam
key_terms.الْخُمُسُ: One-fifth, a specific portion of booty allocated for divine purposes
key_terms.الْمُشْرِكِينَ: Polytheists, those who associate partners with God
key_terms.غَنَائِمَ: War booty or spoils of war

ai.seo_question: How is war booty distributed in Shia jurisprudence when a battalion does or does not engage in combat?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between active combatants and those who merely transport or secure booty, a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding the distribution of ghanimah. It establishes that the five-fold division (khums) applies only when fighting occurs under an Imam-appointed commander, whereas non-combatant acquisition results in the entire booty becoming the exclusive property of the Imam for discretionary distribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The battalion which the Imam<sup>asws</sup> sends, so they acquire war booty, would it be distributed?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If they fought over it with a commander whom the Imam<sup>asws</sup> appointed as a commander over them, one-fifth would be taken out from it for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and for the Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, and four-fifths would be distributed between them. And if they did not happen to have fought the Polytheists over it, everything which they have acquired would be for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> would make it to be wherever he<sup>asws</sup> likes to’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘The Imam dispatches a small armed group against the enemy and they capture properties from the enemy. How should they distribute it?’

He (the Imam) replied, ‘If they fight under the command of a commander appointed by the Imam they should keep aside one-fifth thereof and distribute the rest among themselves. If they have not fought the pagans, then all that they have captured belongs to the Imam who distributes as he finds proper.”’
